edit.description: the `render-refused` arm reads true for both writers

summary: The rendered `render-refused` block reads true for both writers — an unresolved inline-exec span and a pre-invocation hook that threw
acceptance: A hook-refused retry's `<prior-attempt>` block names no inline-exec span and asks for no command removal; the span writer's block still carries its failing spans and their stderr.
tests: the render-refused prior-attempt block does not send a hook-refused retry to fix an inline-exec span
notes: `NO_COMMIT_MODES`' doc and `RenderRefusedAttempt` already name both writers (`spec/chain.md`, *What a hook receives*); only the renderer arm still reads spans-only, so a `promptArgs` throw sends the retry after a span that does not exist. The record carries no discriminant — one `failures` string — so the fix is neutral wording over both writers, not a new field. `RENDER_REFUSED_INTRO` (tests/Dispatcher.test.ts) tracks the intro.

edit.description: shrink the `job new` runtime-ignore roster to a pointer

summary: Shrink `docs/CLI.md`'s `flume job new` runtime-ignore roster to a pointer at `spec/jobs.md`, *Runtime ignores*

per.section: Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source

acceptance: The `job new` bullet names no line of the ignore set and cites the section that owns it; the surrounding claims about merge semantics and chain-convention dirs still read standing alone.
notes: Sibling of the shipped CHAIN-AUTHORING-MANAGED-STATE-POINTS-AT-THE-SPEC, same defect on the CLI guide. The bullet spells six of ten `RUNTIME_IGNORES` names — no `merging/`, `tick-verdict.json`, `tick-verdicts.jsonl`, `stop` — and cites nothing. Two copies stand and are not this entry's: `job status`'s five names already cite and claim what outlives a branch switch; `job rm`'s list illustrates what `git rm` left behind. docs/ reaches no rung above prose, so deleting the copy is the fix.
